nodes.n: Three days after the World Cup semi-final. You lost by four runs. Then somebody posted a photo of you at a party at 3 AM the night before.
"CAPTAIN PARTIES, COUNTRY CRIES." Every channel. Every hour.

nodes.th: I had one drink. I left at midnight. Nobody cares.

nodes.n: A five-star hotel in Bandra, Suite 1104. Your agent said "a meeting that will save your captaincy". He didn't say who with.

nodes.t: Nikhil Arora. I fix images. Yours is broken. So is my client's.
The Board wants a family man. Sponsors want a love story. And the country wants to forgive you. Let's give them a wedding.

nodes.n: The bedroom door opens. Tara Kapoor. Three hundred million followers. Two flops in a row. Barefoot, holding an iced coffee.

nodes.t: So you're the cricketer. You're shorter on TV.
Let's be clear. I don't watch cricket. I don't understand cricket. I think a googly is a type of egg.

choice.t: "A googly is a ball that lies to you. Like this meeting."
"And I don't watch your films. We're even."

nodes.t: One year. Married in public, strangers in private. Separate rooms. You attend her premieres, she attends your matches. Clause twelve: a quiet divorce after twelve months.
Clause seven: no falling in love. It ruins the timeline.

nodes.n: Page nine has a handwritten line, in Tara's writing: "He must never meet my mother alone."

nodes.t: Wonderful. One more rule. Mine, not his.
My mother can never find out it's fake. Never. Promise me.

nodes.cliff: You just married a stranger for one year. And she's more scared of her mother than of the country.
